title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues §10 of Grothendieck's notes on the 'équation des lacets' (the loop equations defining the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group). The setting is a group M_{ρ,σ} built over the profinite modular group, where SL(2,Z)^ is the amalgam generated by an element ρ of order 3 or 6 and an element σ of order 4.

(1) Closing the previous paragraph. The previous page defined two subgroups by setting U = b or U = a:
- M_{ρ,σ}(σ) = {(a,b,U) : U = b};
- M_{ρ,σ}(ρ) = {(a,b,U) : U = a}.
They give partial sections of the projection M_{ρ,σ} → τ_{ρ,σ}. Here τ_{ρ,σ} ⊂ T_ρ × N'_σ is cut out by δ_ρ(a)/δ_σ(b) ∈ μ_n, and τ'_{ρ,σ} = Ker(ε_3: τ_{ρ,σ} → μ_n) = T_ρ ×_{μ_n} N'_σ. Formula (48) gives a further quotient τ'/τ° detected by a character ε_2. The target is probably Ẑ or μ_n; this is illegible.

(2) Remark. These subgroups are 'evident' by definition. They supply sections over τ' as soon as, in the general framework of p. 526' ff, one has embeddings T_ρ ↪ G and N'_σ ↪ G such that δ_ρ and δ_σ are induced by a single δ_G. So the construction is functorial in any ambient group with a compatible character δ.

(3) Modular case. The two subgroups are renamed by the points of the λ-line (cross-ratio line) P^1 − {0,1,∞} that they stabilise:
- M(σ) = M(1/2). The point 1/2 is the harmonic point, fixed by the involution q ↦ 1−q.
- M(ρ) = M(−j). The point −j is the equianharmonic point, a fixed point of the order-3 homography.
From M(0) and M(1/2), Grothendieck defines M(q) for q in {0, 1, ∞} ∪ {1/2, 2, −1} by transport: int(ρ_SG) M(q) = M(ρ̇(q)), with ρ̇(q) = 1/(1−q).
- ρ̇ has order 3, matching ρ̃^3 = 1 in the quotient.
- It permutes the three cusps 0 → 1 → ∞ → 0 and the three harmonic points 1/2 → 2 → −1 → 1/2.
- The margin says ρ_SG is ρ regarded as an element of the copy of SL^(2,Z) (written SG) inside M_{ρ,σ}.

In modern terms, these are 'local' subgroups (decomposition or stabiliser subgroups) attached to the special points of the λ-line. The cusps are the tangential base points. The harmonic and equianharmonic points sit over the elliptic points j = 1728 and j = 0 of M_{1,1}. The anharmonic S_3 = SL_2(Z)/Γ(2)·±1 permutes them.

(4) Open task stated on the page. M(−j) remains to be defined. One must also fix the choice of these subgroups inside a well-determined SL(2,Z)^-conjugacy class, because the subgroups are only canonical up to conjugation. The next page proposes candidates int(σ_i)(M(0)) for i ∈ {0, 1, ∞}.
errors: The orbit of 1/2 under q ↦ 1/(1−q) is {1/2, 2, −1}, not {1/2, −2, −1}. Either the transcription misreads '2' as '−2', or the manuscript has a slip.
The remark writes 'δ_σ, δ_σ'; it should read 'δ_ρ, δ_σ' (induced by δ_G).
−j is a fixed point of ρ̇ only if j denotes a primitive cube root of unity with −j = e^{±iπ/3}. This is consistent, but M(−j) is left undefined, as Grothendieck himself notes.

ideas.what: Indexing subgroups of an extension of SL(2,Z)^ by the special points {0,1,∞}, {1/2,2,−1}, {−j} of the λ-line, transported by the order-3 homography q ↦ 1/(1−q) (anharmonic S_3 action)
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition/inertia subgroups at tangential base points and at orbifold (elliptic) points of M_{0,4}/S_3 ≅ M_{1,1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara and Nakamura (tangential base points and Galois action on π_1 of M_{0,4} and M_{1,1}); Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps and Schneps (GT and the orbifold points of M_{1,1})
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{1,1}, M_{0,4} and the S_3 symmetry in general terms; the explicit M_{ρ,σ}(q) construction seems unpublished

ideas.what: Partial sections M(σ), M(ρ) of M_{ρ,σ} → τ_{ρ,σ} over the fibre product τ' = T_ρ ×_{μ_n} N'_σ, existing whenever T_ρ and N'_σ embed compatibly in a group G with character δ_G
ideas.modern_name: Sections of extensions over fibre products of local (stabiliser) groups; compatible characters

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets the problem of defining canonical subgroups M(−j) and fixing them within a determined SL(2,Z)^-conjugacy class, i.e. a rigidified system of 'local groups' at the elliptic points compatible with the S_3 action. This is a step toward GT-type relations coming from the orbifold points of M_{1,1}.
missed.quote: Il resterait : définir M_{ρ,σ}(−j), et [préciser] le choix : à l'intérieur d'une classe de SL(2,Z)^ conjugaison bien déterminée
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Rigidifying decomposition groups at the elliptic points (j = 0, 1728) is relevant to versions of GT built from M_{1,1} and to the 'ρ, σ' relations. The issue appears in later work, though possibly not in exactly this form.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical continuation, with the indexing of subgroups by special points of the λ-line and transport by the order-3 homography. Interesting as a record of Grothendieck treating the elliptic points of M_{1,1} as base points, but close to ideas later developed (tangential base points, GT and M_{1,1}).
transcription_corrections: 'Ces bi[?]-groupes[?] paraissent en[?] définition' → likely 'Ces sous-groupes paraissent évidents par définition'.
'{+modulo[?] de[?]+} section [-...-] / τ'' → likely 'une section au-dessus de τ'_{ρ,σ}'.
'des plongements[?] T_ρ ↪ G, N'_σ ↪ G'; 'δ_σ, δ_σ' → 'δ_ρ, δ_σ'.
(50): q ∈ {0,1,∞; 1/2, 2, −1}; '−2' is probably '2', check the manuscript.
'ρ̇(q) est[?] où[?]' → 'où ρ̇ est la transformation homographique'.
Last lines: 'Il resterait : définir M_{ρ,σ}(−j), et préciser le choix : à l'intérieur d'une classe de SL(2,Z)^-conjugaison bien déterminée, un choix plus [canonique]'.
Margin: 'ρ_SG est ρ en tant qu'élément du sous-groupe SL^_{ρ,σ} ≃ SG de M_{ρ,σ}'.
(48) target: the symbol after ε_2 is unclear; it may be Ẑ or μ_n.
